prompt:
Edit the attached ORIGINAL bundled concept-sheet template directly, preserving exact1672x941 layout, dark navy backdrop, six3x2 panels, floor grids, border margins, badges01–06. Create six DISTINCT SOFTWARE REQUIREMENTS ANALYST tower CHARACTER concepts. This is a business/systems analyst who gathers stakeholder needs, refines USER STORIES, clarifies scope, documents workflows and acceptance criteria. NOT a data scientist, statistics analyst, mathematician or scientist. NO charts, pie charts, graphs, data bars, prisms, node trees, telescopes, goggles, glasses or pointed brows.
Friendly chunky low-poly robotic Copilot-family tower character: the whole character is a compact head with pale teal shell, chalk trim, deep navy face and two simple cyan capsule eyes, no torso, arms, legs or pedestal. Accessories fitted above/beside the head. Creative structural silhouettes differ substantially between the six. No aggressive eye coverings. Opaque broad colour blocks, neutral soft lighting, exact straight FRONT orthographic view, no perspective dominant side faces. Feasible below2500triangles, no measured mesh claims. Interpret requirements visually through STORIES, CONVERSATION, CLARITY, SCOPE and ACCEPTANCE, using large pictograms rather than tiny words.
01 STORY SCRIBE: friendly softly rectangular head with a broad folded STORY CARD mounted offset behind one side, its top projects above the head. Thick chalk card with a big person silhouette icon and two wide raised writing lines, rounded folded corner. A chunky deep teal pencil/stylus clipped on opposite temple. Silhouette asymmetrical, resembles a thoughtful requirements writer. No arm holding card.
02 NEEDS LISTENER: wide low oval head with a welcoming communications accessory: rounded chalk over-head listening band joins large soft rectangular ear pads, one chunky curved microphone stem at side of cheek well BELOW eye level. Behind top of head, two chunky overlapping fitted speech-bubble plates, a broad teal bubble and smaller chalk reply, integral support touching head. Dominant conversation/listening silhouette. No glasses; microphone is small subordinate piece not covering face.
03 SCOPE KEEPER: compact circular head inside a broad chalk open bracket frame: two thick rounded L-shaped vertical brackets fitted outside temples with top and bottom returns, framing the character's boundaries, open above crown. Crown has single broad teal puzzle tab fitted into a chalk matching slot, simple visible fit. Silhouette wide squared frame with friendly round centre. Meaning negotiating scope and fitting needs, no shield or combat gear.
04 CRITERIA COACH: taller narrow head with ONE substantial rounded checklist board on a short central crown mount. Board has exactly two enormous inset rounded checkbox squares in a vertical column, first with chunky teal tick, second blank; beside each one thick horizontal chalk/teal text bar. Checklist board entirely ABOVE eyes. Head small soft ear caps. Bold vertical silhouette, acceptance criteria, not a stack of data slabs.
05 FLOW GUIDE: broad head with a fitted crescent shoulder/back arch behind crown carrying THREE LARGE chunky process blocks across the top, left rounded square, middle rounded diamond, right rounded square, joined by two SHORT thick horizontal connectors. Big inset simple START DOT, QUESTION MARK and CHECK pictograms. All structurally attached by the arch with no thin wires or floating nodes. Silhouette wide bridge above exposed face. Represents clarifying USER WORKFLOW decisions, not statistical dependency graph. No branching stems.
06 STORY WEAVER: round head with TWO broad gently curved chalk ribbon tabs rising from opposite sides and folding together over crown like a soft bookmark bow, one pale teal tab with a large person icon, one chalk tab with a large heart/need icon; central chunky rounded teal join has a checkmark. Continuous fitted interwoven bands, large clear negative spaces, no pointed wings near eyes. Meaning linking WHO, NEED and VALUE in user stories. No hat, charts or data fan.
Models fully visible at same baseline/perceived scale. CRITICAL text safe zones: top row models and shadows must end by y400; bottom row models end by y795. Keep y410–482 and y805–879 COMPLETELY CLEAR for exact labels added later. Models fill central art areas approx58%panelheight with generous negative space. Number badges untouched. Six cheerful capable varied REQUIREMENTS ANALYST head characters, strong thumbnail silhouettes, never tiny user-interface text.
